paragraphs: This paper tests whether vision transformers need more visual experience than newborn animals to learn object recognition. The researchers compare transformers with newborn chicks under controlled, visually restricted conditions. The central question is whether these models can learn to recognize an object across different views when their experience resembles the limited input available to a young animal.

The chicks were raised in environments containing a single object. To approximate their visual experience, the researchers built virtual chambers and recorded first-person images from agents moving through them. They then trained self-supervised vision transformers on those images, using temporal relationships as a teaching signal.

The transformers learned the same view-invariant recognition tasks as the chicks. Within this experimental setting, they were therefore not more data hungry. The result supports the sufficiency of attention-based learning combined with embodied visual streams for developing animal-like object recognition. Its scope is the controlled learning comparison, rather than a claim that transformers reproduce every aspect of biological learning.
neurips-2023-are-vision-transformers-mor.tldr: Vision transformers trained on simulated chick-like visual experience learned view-invariant object recognition under similarly restricted conditions.

paragraphs: Regularization expresses preferences about which solutions a learning system should favor. This paper asks how an Lq penalty on an entire function can be represented probabilistically. That connection matters for Bayesian modeling of objects such as images, where a prior should express useful structural preferences while supporting uncertainty-aware prediction.

The authors construct the Q-exponential process by extending a scalar q-exponential distribution to consistent multivariate distributions. Consistency is essential because the distributions must fit together as descriptions of one stochastic process. Their construction draws on elliptically contoured distributions and connects to Besov processes, offering an explicit probabilistic formulation, direct control over correlation strength, and a tractable prediction formula.

The resulting process provides a flexible prior over functions. For q below two, it supplies a sharper penalty than the Gaussian-process case at q equal to two. Comparisons with Gaussian and Besov processes on functional data, image reconstruction, and inverse problems demonstrate advantages for the proposed methodology. The contribution links a familiar regularization idea to a usable probabilistic model of functions.
neurips-2023-bayesian-learning-via-q-exp.tldr: Q-exponential processes turn Lq function regularization into a flexible Bayesian prior with explicit correlations and tractable prediction.

paragraphs: Text-to-image diffusion models contain useful visual knowledge for generation and editing. Applying that knowledge to videos, panoramas, or three-dimensional scenes creates an additional challenge: several related images must agree with one another. An edit that works for an individual image does not by itself solve consistency across the complete visual representation.

Collaborative Score Distillation addresses this by updating multiple samples together. The method builds on Stein Variational Gradient Descent, treating the samples as interacting particles. It combines their score functions so that the diffusion model's generative guidance is distilled across the image collection synchronously. This provides a mechanism for information to pass between samples during editing.

The researchers demonstrate the method on panorama, video, and three-dimensional scene editing. Their results support its ability to improve consistency between samples across these different applications. The approach matters because it adapts image-based generative knowledge to tasks whose success depends on relationships among images, extending the usefulness of text-to-image models beyond isolated outputs.
neurips-2023-collaborative-score-distill.tldr: Collaborative Score Distillation jointly guides related images to improve consistency in panorama, video, and 3D scene editing.

paragraphs: Best-arm identification asks which available option has the highest average reward while using as few observations as possible. In the fixed-confidence setting studied here, the learner receives an error tolerance, delta, and must identify the best option with probability at least one minus delta. The paper broadens the usual setting by allowing rewards from different options to be dependent.

The key additional capability is simultaneous sampling of rewards. This lets the learner estimate covariance: information about how the outcomes of different options vary together. The proposed algorithms adapt to this initially unknown dependence structure. Rather than treating every option's observations as unrelated, they use relationships among outcomes to make identification more efficient.

The authors provide theoretical guarantees showing that substantial improvements over the standard setting can be achieved. They also derive lower bounds for the relaxed setting and present numerical simulations supporting the theory. The contribution is therefore both algorithmic and foundational: it explains how correlated observations can help and establishes constraints on what identification procedures can accomplish.
neurips-2023-covariance-adaptive-best-ar.tldr: Algorithms that learn correlations among simultaneously sampled rewards can identify the best option more efficiently at a specified confidence level.

paragraphs: Image-processing networks commonly work with spatial information or frequency information as separate perspectives. This paper introduces the Fractional Fourier Transform as a continuous, unified way to examine both. The motivation is to give models a richer view of image signals, particularly when their characteristics vary across the image rather than remaining stationary.

The researchers study the transform's image-processing properties and develop a fast two-dimensional implementation. They then build Multi-order Fractional Fourier Convolution, or MFRFC, an operator that processes images from multiple perspectives within the spatial-frequency plane. Its role is to serve as a reusable component that can be integrated into models for different vision tasks.

Experiments cover object detection, image classification, guided super-resolution, denoising, dehazing, deraining, and low-light enhancement. The authors report significant improvements over baseline methods across all of these evaluated tasks. The breadth of that result supports the proposed operator's usefulness as a general image-processing building block, connecting the unified representation to practical gains across recognition and restoration.
neurips-2023-deep-fractional-fourier-tra.tldr: A multi-order Fractional Fourier convolution combines spatial and frequency perspectives and improves performance across several evaluated vision tasks.

paragraphs: World models simulate possible futures for model-based reinforcement learning agents. When the environment is only partially observable, useful simulations require memory of information that may no longer be visible. This paper investigates whether alternatives to recurrent neural networks can improve that memory, focusing on transformers and Structured State Space Sequence models, known as S4.

The authors introduce S4WM, a world model compatible with parallelizable state-space models. It combines this sequence-processing backbone with latent-variable modeling, allowing high-dimensional image sequences to be generated through latent imagination. They also compare recurrent, transformer, and S4 world models in four sets of environments designed to test distinct memory capabilities.

Those assessments cover long-term imagination, context-dependent recall, reward prediction, and memory-based reasoning. In the reported comparisons, S4WM offers stronger long-term memory than transformer-based world models while being more efficient during training and imagination. These findings identify a promising backbone for future model-based agents, with the demonstrated contribution centered on the quality and efficiency of their world models.
neurips-2023-facing-off-world-model-back.tldr: S4WM improves long-term memory and efficiency over transformer world models in environments designed to test memory capabilities.

paragraphs: Continuous diffusion models have a deterministic probability-flow description, but an analogous description has been missing for discrete diffusion models. This paper develops a theoretical foundation for that discrete counterpart. The aim is to connect how probability distributions evolve during diffusion with optimal transport, a framework for moving probability mass between distributions.

The authors first prove that continuous probability flow corresponds to a Monge optimal transport map under certain conditions. They also present corresponding evidence for discrete cases. These connections motivate their definition of discrete probability flow through optimal-transport principles. The conditional nature of the continuous result is part of the theoretical claim, rather than an unrestricted equivalence.

Building on that definition, the paper proposes a sampling method that produces more certain outcomes than previous discrete diffusion models. Experiments on a synthetic toy dataset and CIFAR-10 support the effectiveness of the proposed flow. The contribution combines a mathematical formulation with a practical sampling procedure, showing how the transport perspective can inform discrete generation.
neurips-2023-formulating-discrete-probab.tldr: The paper defines discrete diffusion probability flow through optimal transport and uses it to sample more certain outcomes.

paragraphs: Changing training batch size can reduce elapsed training time, but preserving learning behavior requires adjusting the optimization process. This paper examines a component that earlier scaling approaches overlooked: the exponential moving average of model parameters. This moving-average model follows the target model at a rate controlled by a momentum parameter and can influence both predictions and learning.

The authors provide a scaling rule for optimization involving a model EMA. They validate it across multiple architectures, optimizers, and data modalities. They also examine settings where the moving-average model helps train the target model, including pseudo-labeling and self-supervised learning. In these settings, maintaining its behavior matters for the learning signal itself.

The rule enables EMA-based methods to operate at both small and large batch sizes. For BYOL, the authors report training at a batch size of 24,576 without sacrificing performance. They associate this with a sixfold wall-clock reduction under idealized hardware conditions. That qualification matters: the result demonstrates the scaling opportunity without promising the same speedup on every hardware setup.
neurips-2023-how-to-scale-your-ema-2a61b.tldr: An EMA-aware scaling rule preserves training behavior across batch sizes and enables larger-batch self-supervised learning without reported performance loss.

paragraphs: Personalizing a text-to-image model requires more than teaching it a person's appearance. The new identity also needs to combine effectively with other concepts in text prompts. This paper targets that combination ability, which the authors describe as weaker for identities added by previous customization methods than for concepts already present in the pretrained model.

Their method builds a celebrity-based basis within the pretrained text encoder's embedding space. Given one facial photograph, it learns weights over that basis to produce an embedding for the target identity. All other parameters stay fixed. The reported customization uses 1,024 learnable parameters and takes less than three minutes.

The authors report better combination of the new identity with other concepts than previous personalization methods. They also demonstrate learning several identities together and generating interactions among them. The approach matters because it places a new identity within an existing representational space, supporting prompted combinations while requiring only a small amount of identity-specific training and a single input photograph.
neurips-2023-inserting-anybody-in-diffus.tldr: Celeb Basis personalizes a diffusion model from one facial photo by learning a compact identity embedding with improved concept-combination ability.

paragraphs: Traditional supervised recognition assigns examples to a category set established during training. Discovering unfamiliar categories at test time requires a way to decide what should count as a category in the first place. This paper approaches that question through optimization, defining a category in terms of an optimal solution to a specified problem.

The resulting method is self-supervised and assigns minimum-length category codes to individual examples. These codes capture an implicit hierarchy among categories in the data. That hierarchy matters because categorization can operate at different levels of detail, and the coding mechanism gives the model greater control over how finely it distinguishes groups.

The authors report effective discovery of unknown categories in experimental comparisons with state-of-the-art benchmarks, including handling fine-grained categories. They also provide a proof of optimality for their formulation. Together, the theoretical and empirical contributions connect a formal definition of categories with a practical discovery method, making category granularity part of the learning approach rather than simply accepting a fixed label inventory.
neurips-2023-learn-to-categorize-or-cate.tldr: Self-coding discovers unknown categories using minimum-length codes that represent category hierarchy and provide control over granularity.

paragraphs: This paper studies learning large Gaussian graphical models under the mathematical constraint called multivariate total positivity of order two, or MTP2. Its focus is computational: a large optimization problem can be expensive even when the underlying graph is sparse. The authors look for graph structure that allows the work to be divided without changing the problem being solved.

Their method uses bridges in the thresholded sample covariance graph. A bridge is a connection whose removal separates parts of a graph. The authors prove that a bridge-block decomposition turns the original optimization into smaller subproblems, together with explicit solutions for entries associated with bridges. The decomposition is an equivalent reformulation of the full problem.

This provides a way to apply existing algorithms to smaller, more tractable pieces while handling bridge entries directly. The authors report substantial computational reductions and significant speedups over state-of-the-art benchmarks on synthetic and real-world data. The key contribution is a provable decomposition strategy that can improve the computational efficiency of existing methods for this model class.
neurips-2023-learning-large-scale-mtp-2-.tldr: A provably equivalent bridge-block decomposition accelerates learning of large MTP2 Gaussian graphical models by splitting them into smaller problems.

paragraphs: An open-world classifier needs to recognize when an input belongs to a class outside its training categories. Auxiliary examples of out-of-distribution data can help, but they may differ from the unfamiliar data encountered later. This paper studies that mismatch through learning theory and identifies distribution discrepancy as a key influence on detection performance.

The proposed Distributional-Augmented OOD Learning method, or DAOL, expands training beyond one auxiliary distribution. It constructs a set of distributions inside a Wasserstein ball centered on the available auxiliary OOD distribution. The predictor is then trained against the worst OOD data within that set, accounting for a range of distributional alternatives.

The authors justify that this worst-case training can reduce the relevant discrepancy and improve open-world detection using only the auxiliary OOD data. Evaluations across representative detection settings report better performance than advanced competing methods. The approach matters because it treats uncertainty about future unfamiliar inputs as a distribution-level training problem, directly addressing the gap between available auxiliary examples and later OOD encounters.
neurips-2023-learning-to-augment-distrib.tldr: DAOL trains against distributional variations around auxiliary OOD data to improve detection of unfamiliar inputs encountered later.

paragraphs: Language models sometimes fall into repetitive, uninformative loops. This paper examines that behavior from the perspective of training data, offering a common explanation for several previously proposed accounts. Its preliminary investigation finds a strong correlation between repeated material in the training data and repetition during generation.

The researchers then intervene during training by selectively dropping attention to repetitive words. Their experiments show that this can substantially reduce degeneration. This gives the data-centered explanation support beyond the initial correlation: changing how the model learns from repeated words changes the unwanted generation behavior.

The paper also empirically reexamines earlier approaches involving high-inflow words, the likelihood objective, and self-reinforcement. It argues that penalizing training-data repetition is a shared factor behind their effectiveness. Additional experiments find that such penalties remain important with larger models and instruction tuning. The findings position repetition in training as a useful target for intervention and a unifying interpretation of existing remedies, without establishing it as the only possible cause of degeneration.
neurips-2023-repetition-in-repetition-ou.tldr: Experiments link repetitive generation to training-data repetition and show that reducing attention to repeated words can substantially mitigate it.

paragraphs: Many fairness, robustness, and safety objectives ask a model to perform well under an unfavorable data distribution. This paper brings such objectives into a shared framework called Responsible AI games. The learner minimizes its worst-case loss over a predefined uncertainty set, which may contain perturbed versions of the observed data distribution.

This creates a min-max problem: learning seeks a good model while accounting for the most challenging distribution allowed by the set. The authors offer two algorithm families. One draws on game play, online learning, and game theory. The other builds solutions through greedy stages, drawing on statistical ideas from boosting and regression.

The researchers empirically demonstrate applicability and competitive performance across several responsible-AI problems, particularly those involving subpopulation shift. The framework matters because it lets different objectives share an optimization language and solution methods. Its worst-case protection is defined relative to the chosen uncertainty set, so the distributions included in that set remain central to what the learning objective actually addresses.
neurips-2023-responsible-ai-rai-games-an.tldr: Responsible AI games unify worst-case distributional objectives and provide game-play and greedy stagewise algorithms with competitive empirical performance.

paragraphs: Open-vocabulary object detection benefits from pretrained vision-language models, but learning to locate objects still depends on available detection data. This paper expands that data through self-training: an existing detector generates approximate bounding-box annotations for web image-text pairs. The goal is to make localization training possible at a scale closer to image-level pretraining.

The authors introduce the OWLv2 model and OWL-ST training recipe to address label-space selection, filtering of generated annotations, and training efficiency. OWLv2 exceeds previous state-of-the-art detectors at a comparable scale of roughly ten million examples. OWL-ST then enables training with more than one billion examples, producing further improvements.

With an L/14 architecture, the reported average precision on rare LVIS classes rises from 31.2% to 44.6%, a 43% relative improvement. Those classes have no human-provided box annotations seen by the model. The result demonstrates how automatically generated localization supervision can substantially expand detection training and improve performance on classes lacking that form of human annotation.
neurips-2023-scaling-open-vocabulary-obj.tldr: OWLv2 and OWL-ST scale detector-generated box supervision beyond one billion examples, substantially improving rare-class open-vocabulary detection.

paragraphs: Fine-tuning a pretrained language model can introduce malicious prediction behavior when some training examples have been poisoned. This paper develops a defensive tuning procedure intended to resist that problem whether or not poisoned samples are present. Its central idea is to add a honeypot module designed to capture backdoor information.

The design follows the authors' observation that lower-layer representations contain sufficient backdoor features while carrying little information about the intended task. The honeypot targets that information, and penalties based on what it acquires are used to inhibit backdoor formation in the main network during fine-tuning. This links the defense to a particular observed separation in the model's representations.

Benchmark experiments support the strategy's effectiveness and robustness. The abstract reports attack-success-rate reductions ranging from 10% to 40% compared with previous state-of-the-art methods. These results support improved resistance to attacks in the evaluated settings. Although the stated objective is a backdoor-free model, the reported finding is a reduction in attack success rather than a universal guarantee that every backdoor is eliminated.
neurips-2023-setting-the-trap-capturing-.tldr: A honeypot module captures backdoor-related information during fine-tuning and helps reduce attack success in benchmark evaluations.

paragraphs: Detecting a sound involves identifying when it occurs, while localization estimates the direction it comes from. This paper combines those tasks with visual information, motivated by the fact that sound-producing objects are often visible. Its audio-visual task uses microphone-array recordings and video to estimate both sound-event activity and direction of arrival.

The authors introduce STARSS23, a dataset containing multichannel audio, video, and sound-event annotations across space and time. Participants receive recording instructions intended to ensure adequate activity and occurrences of sound events. Event timing is annotated by people, while direction labels are based on motion-capture tracking and confirmed by people.

The benchmark results demonstrate benefits from using the visible positions of objects in audio-visual sound-event localization and detection. The contribution provides both a task formulation and data for studying it. By connecting sounds with visual source information, the work creates a concrete setting for evaluating whether the two forms of evidence together improve understanding of where and when sound events happen.
neurips-2023-starss23-an-audio-visual-da.tldr: STARSS23 pairs spatial audio, video, and verified event annotations to study sound detection and localization aided by visual object positions.

paragraphs: Intrinsic images describe scene properties such as depth, surface orientation, albedo, or shading. This paper shows that a pretrained StyleGAN can be induced to generate these property maps for its own images. The finding suggests that a model trained to generate images also represents information about properties underlying their appearance.

The mechanism is a fixed shift in the generator's latent input. For each type of intrinsic image, the authors identify an offset that turns the output associated with a latent code into the corresponding property map. Crucially, that offset does not depend on the original code. The generator was pretrained by others, so this behavior was not created by a special training regime devised for the study.

The resulting maps compare well qualitatively and quantitatively with state-of-the-art image-regression methods and show robustness to relighting effects. The authors also identify transformations that cannot be produced through this offset mechanism. That distinction makes the discovery specific: the generator exposes useful intrinsic-image structure without functioning as a general-purpose image-regression system.
neurips-2023-stylegan-knows-normal-depth.tldr: Fixed latent offsets let a pretrained StyleGAN generate intrinsic property maps that compare well with regression methods and resist relighting effects.

paragraphs: Reinforcement learning agents need to explore, especially when useful external rewards are rare. Intrinsic rewards temporarily supplement those external signals with incentives generated by the agent itself. This paper argues that exploration can benefit from information about how states were reached, alongside information about the future possibilities associated with those states.

Successor-Predecessor Intrinsic Exploration, or SPIE, combines prospective and retrospective information in a new intrinsic reward. The retrospective component draws on the structure of transition sequences. Its purpose is to make exploratory behavior sensitive to the broader organization of the environment, allowing the agent to use global structural information rather than relying only on local prospects.

The authors report more efficient exploration in environments with sparse rewards and bottleneck states, together with behavior they describe as more ethologically plausible than competing methods. They also implement SPIE in deep reinforcement learning agents and find stronger empirical performance on sparse-reward Atari games. These results support combining information about past transitions and future possibilities when designing exploration incentives.
neurips-2023-successor-predecessor-intri.tldr: SPIE combines retrospective and prospective state information to improve exploration in sparse-reward environments.

paragraphs: Survival analysis studies the time until an event occurs. When the variables describing a case change over time, their changing behavior can matter for predicting that event. This paper proposes a nonparametric Bayesian model for capturing nonlinear relationships between time-to-event outcomes and such time-varying covariates.

The model adapts a permanental process to survival data. Its stated modeling assumption places a Gaussian process on the square root of the hazard function, which describes event risk over time. The authors establish a representer-theorem property and use it to develop a fast Bayesian estimation algorithm. The computation avoids Markov chain Monte Carlo and scales linearly with the number of observed events.

Evaluations on synthetic and real-world data show predictive accuracy comparable to state-of-the-art methods while running tens to hundreds of times faster. The contribution is therefore a combination of flexible statistical modeling and computational efficiency. It offers a way to account for changing covariates and nonlinear dependence without the computational cost of the compared estimation methods.
neurips-2023-survival-permanental-proces.tldr: A Bayesian permanental-process survival model handles time-varying covariates with comparable predictive accuracy and substantially faster reported estimation.

paragraphs: Complex reasoning over a knowledge graph may require following several relationships and combining logical conditions. When facts also carry time information, the query may ask for an entity or a timestamp. This paper addresses that temporal setting, where reasoning must combine operations on sets of entities with operations on sets of times.

The proposed Temporal Feature-Logic Embedding framework, TFLEX, represents complex temporal queries in an embedding space. It uses fuzzy logic for the logical component of its representations, supporting first-order logic operations over entity sets. The authors extend this treatment to timestamp sets and add temporal operators for After, Before, and Between.

Experiments across numerous query patterns demonstrate the method's effectiveness. The contribution brings entity-based and time-based reasoning into one framework, addressing a gap left by approaches focused on static knowledge graphs. Its significance lies in making temporal conditions part of the query operations themselves, so multi-hop questions can seek answers about both which entities satisfy a query and when its conditions hold.
neurips-2023-tflex-temporal-feature-logi.tldr: TFLEX combines entity logic with temporal operators to answer complex multi-hop queries over temporal knowledge graphs.

paragraphs: Step-by-step prompting can improve language-model problem solving, but directly supervising those steps requires costly written rationales. This paper proposes training from correct answers while treating the rationale as an unobserved variable. The objective approximately averages over possible rationales when maximizing the likelihood of producing the correct answer.

The main technical challenge is sampling rationales conditioned on that answer. The authors use a Markov chain Monte Carlo expectation-maximization algorithm, drawing inspiration from STaR and several latent-variable learning methods. They also introduce a control-variate technique that reduces noise in gradient estimates, with variance tending to zero as the model improves.

On GSM8K and BIG-Bench Hard tasks, this training method typically improves held-out accuracy more than STaR or prompt-tuning with or without chain-of-thought. The qualification matters: the reported advantage is typical across the evaluation, rather than universal. The approach offers a way to improve reasoning-oriented performance without requiring people to annotate detailed rationales, using probabilistic inference to connect possible reasoning paths with known correct answers.
neurips-2023-training-chain-of-thought-v.tldr: MCMC-EM fine-tuning treats rationales as latent variables and typically improves reasoning-task accuracy without manually labeled reasoning steps.

paragraphs: Graph neural architecture search usually relies on labels to judge which network designs work well. This paper studies how to perform that search when only unlabeled graphs are available. Its central challenge is that the underlying factors shaping graph data and the architectures suited to those factors are intertwined.

The proposed DSGAS method builds a graph super-network containing multiple architectures, with separate treatment of latent factors. These architectures are optimized together. A self-supervised training procedure jointly disentangles graph and architecture information to estimate performance under different factors. A contrastive search process using architecture augmentations then seeks designs with factor-specific expertise.

Experiments on eleven real-world datasets show state-of-the-art performance against several baselines without supervised labels during the search. The approach matters because it supplies a learning signal for architecture selection where conventional labeled evaluation is unavailable. It also treats variation in the graph's latent factors as information for finding suitable architectures, making their relationship part of the search process rather than leaving it entangled.
neurips-2023-unsupervised-graph-neural-a.tldr: DSGAS searches for graph neural architectures without labels by disentangling latent graph factors and learning factor-specific architectural expertise.

paragraphs: Video understanding can draw on images, sound, and subtitles, yet video-text foundation models have emphasized vision and text. This paper develops a dataset and model that connect all three video tracks with textual descriptions. The goal is to make audio and subtitles more fully available to the model's understanding of video.

To build VAST-27M, the researchers collect 27 million open-domain clips and train separate vision and audio captioners. An existing large language model then integrates those generated descriptions with subtitles and instructional prompts to produce captions spanning the modalities. The resulting automatically generated corpus is used to train the VAST foundation model.

VAST processes visual, audio, and subtitle information and supports vision-text, audio-text, and multimodal video-text tasks, including retrieval, captioning, and question answering. The authors report 22 state-of-the-art results across cross-modality benchmarks. These findings support the usefulness of both the corpus and the model, demonstrating the practical value of training video-text systems with descriptions that incorporate multiple information streams.
neurips-2023-vast-a-vision-audio-subtitl.tldr: VAST combines vision, audio, and subtitles through a 27-million-video caption corpus, achieving 22 reported state-of-the-art cross-modality results.

paragraphs: Semantic segmentation assigns category labels across an image, but obtaining training annotations takes substantial effort, and generalizing to unseen classes remains difficult. Zero-shot segmentation uses large vision-language models to transfer to classes without task-specific training on them. This paper asks how to evaluate that ability across a broad range of specialized application domains.

The authors create MESS, a benchmark for multi-domain evaluation. They review 120 datasets, develop a taxonomy for organizing them, and classify the datasets with it. From that collection, they select 22 representative datasets spanning areas such as medicine, engineering, earth monitoring, biology, and agriculture.

They evaluate eight recently published models on the benchmark and analyze characteristics associated with zero-shot transfer performance. The contribution is a structured evaluation resource and comparative analysis, giving researchers a broader basis for studying generalization across domains. The taxonomy and representative selection make dataset coverage an explicit part of the evaluation design, helping frame zero-shot segmentation as a question spanning many kinds of imagery.
neurips-2023-what-a-mess-multi-domain-ev.tldr: MESS evaluates eight zero-shot segmentation models on 22 representative datasets selected through a taxonomy of 120 reviewed datasets.
